rules.name: SWIFTNESS OF LIGHTNING
rules.text: For every [Air] you have, you may use 1 [Slow] Power as if it were [Fast] . (Power Cards or your Innate Powers.)
rules.turn:
made-fast S P T, turn T / speed P fast

fast-phase, spirit:special S swiftness-of-lightning, ~swiftness S
swiftness S, elements S air A, made-fast-count S U, lt U A
  ?[rng] P
  !(swift-option S P)
  ~swift-choice S P
fast-phase, turn T, >swift-choice S C, is C P, played S P
  +made-fast S P T
  ~>use-power S P
  ~swiftness S
rules.evidence: seeds 7/3/11 with 2 Air and 3 Slow cards: exactly two cards get made-fast and use-power in the Fast phase; the third resolves in the Slow phase; no card resolves twice
rules.notes: Speed is an @last acc, so "as if it were Fast" is a later contribution and the base Slow phase skips the card on its own (One Use!). The Air count is re-read on every use, as the FAQ requires. First attempt made the same card Fast twice: the continuation ran inside swift-choice, before made-fast existed; `fast-phase, >swift-choice` fixed it. Innate Powers are not modeled. Port to fresh-left `^` (v2-caret-fresh-left): `^made-fast` from a separate `turn` rule started at a moment incomparable with the next `swiftness`, so the count never saw it; `made-fast` is now asserted in the chain that uses the Power and asks again, and names its turn so the speed override lasts exactly that turn.

language_issues: A rule's continuation runs inside the episode it first matched, so reads there cannot see facts that start when that episode ends; nothing warns about it (fix: `parent, >ep, ...`).
